haiku-low.q1: It persists only a SHA-256 hash (token_hash) in api_tokens. Plaintext appears once, in the 201 create response, held in dialog memory only. Never written to database, logs or analytics.
haiku-low.q2: They cannot. Plaintext is never stored or re-shown, nobody can show it again, including support. The user must create a new token.
haiku-low.q3: The create is refused with 409 and the message: "You already have 10 active tokens. Revoke one before creating another."
haiku-low.q4: On the next API request with that token, because nothing caches validity. That request gets a 401.
haiku-low.q5: All three get the same 401 with {"error":"unauthorized"} and the same headers. The responses do not differ.
haiku-low.q6: The server SHA-256 hashes the presented token and looks up the row by token_hash in Postgres. Usable if revoked_at is empty and expires_at has not passed.
haiku-low.q7: Each valid API call records the token id and time in memory; a 5-minute batch flush writes it. Document does not state a once-per-hour cap mechanism.
haiku-low.q8: The request is not failed. The buffer keeps its entries and retries on the next cycle; last-used data may lag, within the 1-hour allowance.
haiku-low.q9: Revoking sets revoked_at to now on the user's own token row. The list then excludes it, since it shows only active, unrevoked, unexpired tokens.
haiku-low.q10: Another user's or a missing token id returns 404. Revoking a token this user already revoked returns 200, so retries are safe.
haiku-low.q11: A row exists, counts toward the limit, and shows Never, but nobody holds the token. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key gets 409. User must revoke it and create a new one.

sonnet.q1: Only the SHA-256 hash (token_hash) is stored in Postgres. The plaintext exists in server memory when made, in the body of the one 201 create response, and in the browser dialog's memory until the dialog closes. It is never in the database, logs or analytics.
sonnet.q2: They cannot. The token is shown once and nobody (including support and engineering) can show it again. The user must create a new token.
sonnet.q3: The server refuses with 409 'limit reached' and the message 'You already have 10 active tokens. Revoke one before creating another.' The count check and insert run in one transaction under a row lock.
sonnet.q4: On the very next API request with that token, because no cache holds validity and each call reads revoked_at from Postgres by hash.
sonnet.q5: Every case gets 401 with body {"error":"unauthorized"} and the same headers (WWW-Authenticate: Bearer). The responses do not differ, and all go through the same hash-and-lookup path.
sonnet.q6: The server parses the Authorization header, computes the SHA-256 of the presented token, and looks up the api_tokens row by token_hash. The row is usable if it exists and revoked_at is empty and expires_at has not passed.
sonnet.q7: A valid API call records the token id and current time in the in-memory last-used buffer. The buffer is flushed to Postgres every 5 minutes in one batch UPDATE using GREATEST. The document does not state any mechanism limiting writes to at most one per token per hour; it says the 1-hour figure is an allowance for staleness. NOT STATED for an hourly write cap.
sonnet.q8: The request is not affected, because last-used is recorded in memory on the request with no DB write. A failed flush keeps the buffer entries and retries next cycle.
sonnet.q9: It sets revoked_at = now on the row (the row stays). The token is then excluded from the list, which shows only rows that are not revoked and not expired.
sonnet.q10: If the token id is missing or owned by another user, the response is 404 (same as missing). If this user already revoked it, the response is 200 (retry is safe).
sonnet.q11: The row exists in Postgres but nobody holds the plaintext and the server cannot resend it. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key gets 409 with no token. The stranded row counts toward the 10 limit and shows 'Never' for last-used until revoked or 90 days pass. The user recovers by revoking the stranded token and creating a new one. An ack call plus 15-minute sweep is a recommended but undecided fix.
